subject.title: [Bug]: openclaw status falsely reports openclaw-mem0 memory as unavailable when the live gateway plugin is working

question: Should memory status be resolved from live gateway runtime health, from a passive local plugin-status contract, or is the current `not checked` mitigation sufficient for this issue?
rationale: Current main softened the misleading wording but did not implement the live-runtime health contract requested here, and the open fork PR plus https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/62599 require an owner decision about the permanent status boundary.

options.title: Use the broader live-gateway contract
options.body: Make https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/62599 the canonical implementation path, close or replace the conflicting fork PR, and require live external-memory proof before closing this issue.

options.title: Revive the fork PR
options.body: Ask the fork PR author to rebase, resolve conflicts, and prove `status --deep` plus JSON output against a real external memory plugin without local plugin side effects.

options.title: Accept `not checked` as sufficient
options.body: Declare the shipped softened wording enough for this report, close the conflicting fork PR, and close this issue with release evidence.

recommendation.title: Use the broader live-gateway contract
recommendation.body: Make https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/62599 the canonical implementation path, close or replace the conflicting fork PR, and require live external-memory proof before closing this issue.

likelyOwner.reason: Peter has the strongest file-history signal across the status, plugin memory runtime, and gateway doctor surfaces that need the product-boundary decision.
